- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 3-day avg), cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) or shows strong divergence from price trend, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 7–14 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in 3–5 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) for 3–7 day forecasts.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 30-day MA for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 7 days.
